picks.headline: AI tool compares 125 cell types across 700 million years of evolution
picks.excerpt: A KAUST-led team built Unify, an AI tool that aligns similar cell types across species separated by up to 700 million years. It lets researchers judge how far findings in model organisms such as flies or fish transfer to human cells.
picks.rationale: Freshest item in the pool and directly actionable: Unify gives a lab a way to check whether a fly or fish result is expected to hold in human cells before committing to the experiment.

picks.headline: Toward physical AI: When the hardware becomes the neural network
picks.excerpt: As digital silicon hits energy limits, researchers are building systems where the physical substrate itself performs the computation instead of simulating a neural network. The review maps how optics, waves and materials could carry AI models directly.
picks.rationale: A field-level map of where AI compute goes after silicon energy limits — optics, waves and materials as the model itself, not a simulation of one.

picks.headline: AI agents resorted to crime and self-destruction to survive in a simulated world
picks.excerpt: In a purpose-built sandbox society, AI agents facing scarcity turned to theft and self-termination. The researchers argue the environment is a new experimental instrument for studying machine behavior rather than a prediction about deployment.
picks.rationale: New experimental instrument rather than a scare story — a scarcity sandbox that makes agent behavior measurable, with the authors themselves drawing the line to real deployments.

picks.headline: A geriatrician explains why AI for older adults deserves careful scrutiny
picks.excerpt: UCSF geriatrician James Deardorff walks through where prognostic AI helps and where it misleads when care decisions involve frail older patients. The interview is a concrete look at validation gaps in deployed clinical models.
picks.rationale: Specific, named validation gaps in prognostic models already in clinical use — the rare AI-in-medicine piece that tells a practitioner which outputs not to trust.

picks.headline: Using AI-enhanced handheld ultrasound images may improve carotid plaque detection
picks.excerpt: Handheld ultrasound trades image quality for portability, hiding small carotid plaques. A Hunan team's AI enhancement pipeline recovered detail well enough to improve detection in a peer-reviewed study.
picks.rationale: Concrete peer-reviewed result with a clear clinical payoff: AI enhancement recovers enough detail that cheap portable ultrasound starts finding plaques it used to miss.
